subject: Traffic handoff required — targeted regional cloud disruption and manual routing steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Eliot Kim <eliot@brightcart.com>, J. Alvarez <jalvarez@finedge.co>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Dec 2029 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: Traffic handoff required — targeted regional cloud disruption and manual routing steps

Hi Eliot / Joel —

Short version: we observed an incremental, targeted control-plane degradation impacting our us-west and eu-central serving clusters starting at 08:40 PST this morning. User-facing inference endpoints remained reachable for the majority of tenants, but a subset of BrightCart traffic from eu-west and apac regions experienced elevated error rates and token drops.

Immediate ask: during our mitigations we recommend BrightCart manually switch routing for critical online inference calls to the alternate regional endpoint we host (us-east for EU-origin traffic, and eu-central for APAC-origin where latency tolerances allow). Below is an actionable checklist we can follow together.

Quick checklist (attachable checklist also included):
- Step 1 (5–10 min): Confirm the two traffic prefixes to switch in your edge (we will provide CIDR/URL below).
- Step 2 (5–20 min): Temporarily increase request timeout by 200ms to absorb cold-cache penalties.
- Step 3 (15–30 min): Perform rolling switch for 5% -> 25% -> 100% with health checks at each step.
- Step 4: Notify us when at 25% so Redwood can monitor KV-cache effectiveness and drop-in latency.

We will:
- Hold a 30-minute bridge now (joining SRE Ops).
- Provide a one-click perf dashboard slice for BrightCart to watch errors/latency by route.
- Attach a short CSV with most recent bridge logs and the checklist.

CIDR/endpoint references for manual routing:
- us-east-alt: api-alt.us-east.redwood.com
- eu-central-alt: api-alt.eu-central.redwood.com

We know this is disruptive; the team is treating this as a P1 and Ben is already on the remediation path. If you prefer, we can perform the reroute from our side under your authorization (we will need a signed ephemeral consent token).

I'll open the bridge now.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Posting the quick technical summary for the bridge and the manual-runbook.

Root cause (interim): a cascading route-rebalance in the cloud provider control plane caused a subset of ephemeral endpoints to drop session affinity metadata. That broke our KV-cache locality assumptions for ~8% of tenant traffic routed through the affected POPs. The net effect: token cache misses and elevated request retries.

Mitigation already underway:
- We moved impacted tenants to the cold-cache fallback path within 7 minutes of detection (no data loss).
- A temporary preference rule has been pushed to direct new sessions to the alternate regional endpoints (see Marissa's list).
- We have a collector on the bridge producing per-tenant delta metrics; CSV attached.

Manual switch runbook (summary):
1) Update edge route to api-alt.<region> with a 30s DNS TTL.
2) Extend client-side timeouts to +200ms.
3) Ramp traffic 5% / 25% / 100% with 5–10 minute observation windows.
4) If error rate increases by >0.5% absolute at any step rollback to previous step.

Operational contacts:
- Ben Carter (SRE lead) — ben_carter@redwood.com — +1 415-555-0133 (pager: +1-888-555-0101)
- Karthik Iyer (Traffic Routing PM) — karthik_iyer@redwood.com — +1 650-555-0125

We should be careful about long-tail latency for APAC-origin to eu routes; Naomi please confirm whether BrightCart's APAC traffic has strict 250ms p99 SLA.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Eliot Kim <eliot@brightcart.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Dec 2029 16:22:00 -0800
Subject: Post-incident follow-up: targeted region disruption — postmortem draft and next steps

Hi Eliot / Joel,

Thank you for partnering on the manual reroute yesterday — appreciate the quick execution and the verification checks at each ramp. Attached is the postmortem draft (postmortem-draft-20291211.docx) and a short list of recommended config changes for BrightCart to reduce cold-cache impact next time.

Summary highlights:
- Impact window: 2029-12-10T08:40:00Z — 2029-12-10T11:05:00Z for the majority of affected traffic.
- Customer-visible symptoms: increased 5xx rate and token regeneration on eu-origin and apac-origin calls.
- Customer mitigation: BrightCart performed manual reroute to api-alt endpoints as described; Redwood monitored and adjusted KV affinity rules.

Post-incident actions for Redwood (we will own these):
- CTA-1: Add an automated opt-in to our platform to allow Redwood to perform emergency reroutes on customer behalf with a short-lived consent token. ETA: 3 weeks.
- CTA-2: Improve per-tenant cold-cache warmup telemetry and expose a dedicated dashboard slice. ETA: 2 weeks.
- CTA-3: Formalize guidance for acceptable p99 increase when switching regions; publish as part of our routing runbooks. ETA: 1 week.

Recommended actions for BrightCart (optional but suggested):
- Add a 150–250ms buffer to p99 SLA for cross-region reroutes.
- Maintain a two-step traffic transfer plan in your edge (5% -> 25% -> 100%) and add an automated rollback rule.

If the above readout looks good we'll finalize the postmortem and publish the incident link in the customers portal (we can redact internal traces). Let us know if you'd like a recorded 30-minute readout with engineering.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Product Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
